connections.explanation: The ESPF application is due 21 days out, but venue requests need 30 days, so the venue has to be requested before the funding application to keep both on time.
If most of the budget is food, the $10-per-attendee food cap may limit the award well below the $1,500 maximum.

report.directAnswer: Your organization can likely request up to $1,500 per event from the Example Student Programming Fund, as long as it has re-registered for the current academic year. Work backward from the event date: on-campus venue requests need 30 days of notice, and the current guidelines ask for the ESPF application at least 21 days ahead, although an older announcement lists 14 days. Food counts only when it is incidental to the program and is capped at $10 per expected attendee. Expenses are reimbursed after the event, so plan to cover some costs up front.

keyDiscoveries.summary: The ESPF awards up to $1,500 per event, a figure two campus offices agree on.
Only organizations re-registered for the current academic year are eligible.
On-campus venues must be requested at least 30 days in advance.
Current guidelines require the application at least 21 calendar days before the event.
Funds are released only after the event is registered and approved.
Food is allowed only when incidental to the program, capped at $10 per expected attendee.
Reimbursement requests need itemized receipts within 30 days of the event.

planChangingConnections.text: Request the venue first: its 30-day lead time comes before the 21-day funding deadline, and funds are only released for approved events.
